2. Pending hearing of the Rule, the respondents were directed to allow the petitioners to import telecommunication equipment, and operate and broadcast through satellite system. 

 4. On 23-11-01 the JTV submitted a proposal to the respondent No.1, the Ministry of Information, the Government of Bangladesh for setting up and operating both terrestrial and satellite television channels. Upon the application, said Ministry on 5- 2-02 granted a 'No Objection Certificate', in short, NOC to the JTV for opening and operating countrywide terrestrial and satellite television telecasting and broadcasting in the UHF band under their own management. In the NOC, the JTV was asked to obtain approval from the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in respect of necessary frequency and bandwidth within the scope of the “বেসরকারী টেলিভিশন চ্যানেল স্থাপন ও পরিচালনা নীতিমালা- ১৯৯৮ in short, the Technical Policy, 1998. One of the terms of the NOC was that establishment and operation of the proposed telecommunication system shall be subject to the said Policy. 

 11. Then, on 10-3-04 the Commission granted a licence to the JTV for establishment of telecommunication system and import of equipment and allocation of necessary frequency, Annexure-J, Same date, the Committee also issued a demand note for depositing Taka 54,01,01,300, Annexure- J(1) . The JTV on 11-3-04 deposited Taka 1,00,000 .as fee for establishment of a satellite station (Earth, and Taka 1,300 as licence fees for 13 stations (one satellite and twelve terrestrial). By a letter, the JTV also requested the Commission to amend the demand note by fixing lawful charges for four channels which were granted. 

 12. Upon such representation, the JTV received impugned letter dated 22-3-04 issued by the Ministry of Information, which directed the JTV to stop setting up telecommunication system and broadcasting of the programmers, Annexure-A. It also received in quick succession on 10-4-04 impugned letter dated 8-4-04 issued by and on behalf of the Commission cancelling the licence for failing to deposit the entire money as demanded within the time fixed, Annexure-A (1) and on 11-4-04 impugned letter shown to be dated 24-3-04, by which the Committee informed that there was no scope for consideration of the application of the JTV dated 13-2-02 since the demand was made in respect of 12 terrestrial stations and one satellite station. Hence, the Rule Nisi 

 15. The Commission and the committee, respondent Nos. 3 and 4, jointly opposed the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition. In the affidavit, it is stated that the NOC Annexure-B was not a licence granted by the Ministry of Information. A 'No Objection Certificate' was issued to run a television broadcasting stations through satellite and terrestrial channels whereas the licence is required to establish and operate the telecommunication system and the NOC cannot be treated as a substitute of the licence. The Ministry of Information has not yet granted any licence to the JTV. 

 25. It is further stated that NTV Limited vide its letter dated 1-3-03 in compliance with the said Memo dated 19-2-03 imported equipment to set up television channel and sought for a NOC for releasing of the equipment from the Zia International Airport, Dhaka. The Commission accordingly, vide its letter dated 1-6-03, accorded an inspection certificate. Similarly, the Commission granted permission for using Uplink Downlink Satellite Earth Station (UDSES)/Satellite News Gathering (SNG) and also allocation of frequency for satellite broadcasting vide Annexures-(iii), (iv), (v), (vi) & (vii). 

 27. In reply to the supplementary affidavits, the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 submitted an Affidavit- in-Reply. In such affidavit, the Commission has given the breakdown of the charges, levy and fees of the terrestrial and satellite stations as assessed in the demand note dated 10-3-04. 

 28. At the outset, Mr Rafique-ul-Huq, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the JTV, was very candid in not pressing for a decision upon the rates of charges of the terrestrial stations as was assessed by the Committee in the demand note dated 10-3-04 and a direction upon the respondents to allow the JTV importing telecommunication system, and operating and broadcasting through satellite system, in the terms the Rule Nisi was originally obtained for. 

 52. Back to the facts of the case, we find that the JTV on 23-11-01 submitted the proposal to the Ministry of Information, respondent No.1, for setting up and operation of a privately owned terrestrial and satellite television channel. Upon such application, said respondent on 5-2-02 granted a NOC, Annexure-B, to JTV for operation countrywide of both satellite and terrestrial television in the UHF band in their own management under the Technical Policy of 1998. Such NOC was issued subject to the approval of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in respect of allocation of necessary frequency and band width within the scope of the policy. 

 54. Then, after dilly-dallying for more than two years in the exercise of the statutory duties, on 10-3-04 the Commission issued the licence within the meaning of sections 31, 35 and 36 of the Act, Annexure-J, for establishing a telecommunication system and import of the equipment and allocation of necessary frequency. The licence clearly permitted the JTV to establish 12 terrestrial stations at 12 districts of the country and one satellite station at Bashundhara, Dhaka. The Commission also on the same date sent a demand note demanding Taka 54,01,01,300 as fees and charges. Following day i.e. on 11-3-04, the JTV deposited Taka 1,01,300 as licence fees of said thirteen stations and charges of the frequencies for the satellite station as was assessed by the Commission. Same date the JTV also addressed a letter and requested the Commission to reconsider the charges assessed for use of the frequencies for twelve terrestrial stations. 

 57. On close scrutiny of the NOC, we have already found that the Ministry on 5-2-02 issued the 'No Objection Certificate' on the application dated 23-1-01 of the JTV for the establishment and operation of television channel in own private management by installing equipment and constructing buildings with its own towers in UHF and broadcasting in terrestrial system within the scope of the Technical Policy, 1998. It further permitted the JTV to broadcasting the programmes of all sorts of entertainment including news and current affairs in recorded video cassettes through satellite system subject only to certain conditions. 

 "transmission of any message, information, signal, sound, image, or intellectual expression by radio wave, satellite, cable or optical fiber connection for the purpose of receipt by the public, but transmission of anything by internet connection shall not be deemed to be a broadcasting. 

 60. After giving the NOC to “সম্প্রচার” i.e. broadcasting in both satellite and terrestrial system, we could not find any substance or rationale in the submissions of the learned Attorney-General that even after receipt of such NOC the JTV would need further licence for broadcasting of its programmes. Moreover, in Annexures-A and B the Ministry did never make or intend to make any distinction between the NOC and licence rather used the words simultaneously and alternatively. 

 74. It is true that in the demand note dated 10- 3-04, Annexure-J(1) the Commission asked the JTV to deposit the entire amount of Taka 58,01,01,300 within 15 days. On 11-3,-04 the JTV deposited Taka 1,01,300 as charges for the satellite station and licence fees for thirteen stations, satellite and terrestrial. The JTV also requested in writing the Commission for reconsideration of the charges for use of frequencies for twelve terrestrial stations. The Commission declined the request saying that there was no scope for such reconsideration. If such denial of the Commission would have reached the JTV before the cancellation of the licence, the JTV might have tried to manage the money had they wanted to operate the terrestrial stations. But the failure of the JTV in depositing said charges within said fifteen days would not ipso facto entitle the Commission to cancel the licence. 

 79. After receipt of the NOC, the JTV on 13-2- 02 applied for necessary licence and allocation of frequencies. Under section 36(8) of the Act, the Commission was required to dispose of the application within 180 days. But the Commission sat tight on the application for couple of years. Having failed up to the Appellate Division, the Commission on 10-3-04 granted the licence. Such conduct of the Commission in no way suggests that they acted or intended to act in accordance with the law.
